title: Data Engineer Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Convert a data engineer salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks. Includes National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: A data engineer earning $50 per hour working 38 hours a week would have an annual gross salary of $98,800 before super and tax.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from the same date, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated on top of a base hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is 25% of the minimum hourly rate for the classification. For example, if the base rate is $30.00 per hour, the casual rate is $30.00 × 1.25 = $37.50 per hour. The loading is paid for ordinary hours only, not overtime. Always enter the base rate (without loading) into a calculator, then add the 25% separately.

faqs.q: What superannuation rate applies and is it paid on top of the salary?
faqs.a: The superannuation guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by the employer on top of the agreed salary or hourly rate. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert an Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

To estimate your annual gross salary, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. The formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your pay.

### The 38‑Hour Week Assumption

Most full‑time roles in Australia are based on 38 ordinary hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Act and modern awards. When you see a weekly salary figure, it is usually for 38 hours. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, or $26.44 per hour. If you work part‑time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the National Minimum Wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This can help you budget between paydays.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage each year after the Annual Wage Review. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour. However, most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry and classification. For instance, the Manufacturing and Associated Industries Award (MA000104) has Level 1 at $25.74, Level 2 at $27.08, Level 3 at $29.45, and Level 4 at $32.13 per hour (from 1 July 2026). These rates are minimums; many employers pay above them.

For a data engineer salary, award coverage depends on the industry. Data engineers in IT may be covered by the Professional Employees Award or an enterprise agreement. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year. This figure is a useful benchmark for a typical data engineer salary, though actual pay varies by experience, location, and employer.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For example, a casual data engineer on a base rate of $45.00 per hour would receive $56.25 per hour (including loading). The loading applies to ordinary hours only. When using a calculator, always enter the base rate (without loading) and add the 25% separately via a checkbox or manual calculation.

Superannuation is paid by the employer on top of your gross earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings for 2026–27, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra contribution to your super fund. For a data engineer earning $50 per hour, 38 hours per week, the annual super contribution would be 12% of $98,800 = $11,856, paid on top.

## Data Engineer Salary Benchmarks

While there is no single award rate for data engineers, you can use the ABS average weekly earnings as a guide. The full‑time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week suggest an annual salary of around $108,352. Many data engineer roles fall between $90,000 and $130,000 depending on seniority. To convert an hourly offer to annual, use the formula above. For instance, an hourly rate of $55.00 for 38 hours gives $55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680 per year.

Remember that the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) is the legal floor, and most data engineer salaries are well above it. The [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman list minimum rates for awards, but for professional roles you may need to refer to enterprise agreements or market data. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide tax and super figures for the current financial year.

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a data engineer earning $108,352 per year, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $26,000–$27,000, leaving a take‑home pay of around $81,000–$82,000. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

Super and salary packaging can affect your taxable income. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice into super reduces your assessable income. Remember that super is paid on top of your salary, not from it, unless you salary sacrifice.

## Summary

Converting a data engineer salary from hourly to annual is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Use 38 hours for full‑time. Add 25% casual loading if applicable, and remember super is extra. The National Minimum Wage and award rates are the legal minimums, but most data engineers earn well above them. Always check the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) rules and the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide for more examples.
